items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: And Don used to, you know, Don was a good trumpet player too. And he used to tell me, I used to wipe the wetness from my lips sometimes.

ctx.x: After you got to New York. Right.

See? But, I met Don Redman. Well, Don Redman was in the Ubanqi, no. That was Connec's Inn, when I was in school. And, I used to listen to Don Redman come out of the Connec's Inn when I was in school. And when I got to New York, he was one of the first I met. And Don used to, you know, Don was a good trumpet player too. And he used to tell me, I used to wipe the wetness from my lips sometimes. He said oh, don't do it that way. He said wipe it from your mouthpiece. Let is stay there on your lip. You know? Now, that…
tune away and the people weren't playing it anymore. And, he wrote that tune with McKinney's Cotton Pickers through those years.
